properties.statement: THIRD INSTANCE, AND THE FIRST ONE WHERE THE PEOPLE LOSING THE CYCLE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THE DEFECT DOWN. Deliberately NOT a new defect: fact:defect-a-running-server-cannot-say-it-is-stale (2026-08-07) already states this case in almost these words — '--serve-shared is detached on purpose, so every session that restarted RE-ATTACHED TO THE SAME STALE PROCESS and nothing anywhere reported a problem' — and fact:defect-stale-server-reproduced-first-hand-here records the second. This node exists for what those two do NOT say. WHAT HAPPENED, 2026-08-08 late: Anthony went home specifically to restart and pick up the new binary, restarted the session, and the served surface was unchanged. Measured rather than assumed: `describe_schema(from: DesignRule, to: Component)` still answered 'No edge type specifically models DesignRule -> Component' and still showed CONSTRAINS as `from: ["*"]`, minutes after that enumeration was built, gated and pushed. `ps` explains it: the `--serve-shared` daemon has held the graph since 10:16 that morning, while the restart spawned a NEW `--shared` CLIENT (23:50) which attached to it. WHAT IS NEW AND WORTH THE NODE: (1) THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY IS THE THING THAT FAILS. Every prior record treats 'restart' as the escape from a stale server. Under `--shared` a session restart does not touch the daemon, so the remedy silently does nothing and the user reasonably believes it worked. The actual remedy is `--stop-shared`, which appears in NEITHER prior fact. (2) IT COST A WHOLE DAY OF DOGFOODING. Five merged PRs — the seat-liveness fix, both governance detectors, the skill, the enforced tri-state — were built, gated and merged without one of them ever running through a live session, because the daemon predated all of it. The handoff note written that evening had to say 'check the version rather than assume', which is the workaround this requirement exists to abolish. (3) IT WAS CAUGHT ONLY BY DELIBERATE CHECKING. The session tested a schema fact it happened to know had changed. Nothing surfaced it, and a session without that specific memory would have proceeded on a stale surface believing it was current — which is exactly how the four sessions in the 2026-08-07 report drew opposite conclusions from the same true value. WHY THIS IS AN ARGUMENT AND NOT A COMPLAINT: `req:the-server-is-the-authority-on-its-own-currency` has NOTHING SATISFYING IT and has sat among the 0.60 unsatisfied-requirement gaps all day. The fix is not research: `/proc/self/exe` is marked `(deleted)` the moment the binary is replaced, w-6904efa6 demonstrated it live on a real pid, and it is one syscall with no second source and no version-string comparison. THREE INSTANCES ACROSS TWO PROJECTS AND TWO MACHINES, and the third landed on the maintainer. THE HONEST CAVEAT, because recurrence is not automatically corroboration: these three share a cause rather than a method — two were found by noticing an impossible value, this one by testing a remembered fact — so they add weight to the COST, not to the diagnosis, which was already certain.
